scenarios.label: Restaurant roster repair
scenarios.title: A cook called out. The rest of the roster still has to work.
scenarios.description: Follow Elena from a missing Saturday cook to complete staffing alternatives, then see how an explicit priority changes which repair is preferred.
scenarios.contextTitle: Dinner is booked. The roster is already published.
scenarios.context: On Friday morning, Elena learns that a cook cannot work Saturday dinner. Kitchen coverage, employee availability and a labor expense boundary still apply. Reassigning someone can affect another service. Elena needs a complete repair she can discuss with the team, not just a name for the empty shift.
scenarios.scope: Elena, the restaurant, employees, pay rates and roster are fictional. This dedicated SDK-powered worked example checks four supplied complete repairs for one location and the remaining recorded services in one week. It does not generate every possible roster. Earlier hours and adjacent work inform declared limits; these are example policies, not a claim of employment-law compliance. Staff agreement, actual work and external roster publication remain separate from calculation. The report interface is a custom example, not an installed Marketplace workflow.

scenarios.label: Street-team deployment
scenarios.title: A quiet room. A promotion decision before the window closes.
scenarios.description: Follow three connected decisions: choose a supportable promotion, revisit it when staffing changes, and agree what to learn before funding a future push.
scenarios.contextTitle: More guests would help. Another push still needs a reason.
scenarios.context: Alex manages a fictional gentlemen’s club. The room is quiet, a nearby event is about to finish, and he can authorize up to $400 of additional promotion spending. Five staff are available and four must remain inside. The owner wants a better financial result; the floor needs sufficient coverage; promoters want people on outreach and fair credit. Alex needs a supportable commitment now, a current basis if conditions change, and evidence before repeating the expense.
scenarios.scope: Alex, the venue, records and decisions are fictional. The current 1.5.0 calculation workflow checks operating requirements, presents a Decision summary and compares conditional guest thresholds. Alex makes the management choice and obtains specific authorization through the venue’s operating process; calculation does not record or perform those actions. The tool does not predict attendance or establish a measured marketing effect. Deployment charges are fixed for this version; staffing and same-day timing are simplified. Older saved reviews retain their original choice, authorization and review history. Technical sources and historical examples are linked below. Venue-specific roles, source authentication, external authority and a real learning study require their own review.

scenarios.label: Gift-kit readiness
scenarios.title: Gift-kit handoffs. A plan worth checking.
scenarios.description: Follow Leah from a failed recipient journey to a supported correction. Explore a separate rehearsal-policy adaptation, then screen campaigns and continue one operating review through the CLI and SDK.
scenarios.contextTitle: 120 kits. A day to get the decision right.
scenarios.context: Leah must hand over 120 usable gift kits within a one-day preparation window. Marketing needs the recipient journey to work; production needs a complete correction it can perform; finance expects justified expense. Scoped observations, bookings, permissions and a fresh actual rehearsal support different parts of that promise.
scenarios.scope: Leah, campaign owners, observations, quotes and operating records are fictional. The current Marketplace calculation workflows use release 2.3.0; the article supplies its own one-day case rather than inheriting the starter’s shorter deadline. The separate CLI/SDK continuation uses a version-4 calculation workflow around its unchanged version-3 operating app. Its policy is cost-first and plans ten rehearsal minutes under a five-minute minimum. Retained version-2 teaching cases keep their original timings, and the authoring exercise introduces a ten-minute minimum in a separate release. These versions are not interchangeable. Source authentication, authority and physical production remain company responsibilities.
